CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE N S SANJAY GOWDA  -3-  NC: 2024:KHC:45824  MFA No. 2823 of 2019  ORAL JUDGMENT
The claimant, being dissatisfied with the sum of Rs.3,78,720/-, is in appeal.
2. The occurrence of the accident is not in dispute and so also the liability of the insurer to satisfy the compensation.
3. The Tribunal has come to the conclusion that the claimant had suffered a disability to the extent of 10%.

The Doctor who was examined stated that the claimant had suffered an head injury, a facial Suresh vs Ahmed Shariff on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105675197/
2 fracture apart from a fracture to the knee.

The Doctor (who was examined as PW-6) has however,
stated that as a result of the head injury, the petitioner has not lost control of any of his limbs.

4. Moreover, regarding to the fact that the orthopedic surgeon had stated that the claimant had NC:
2024:KHC:45824 suffered disability to an extent of 50% to his right lower limb.
It would be appropriate to treat the disability as 15% to the whole-body.

5. The accident being of the year 2013, and there being no evidence of the actual income of the claimant, a sum of Rs.8,000/- p.m., fixed by the by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority will have to be adopted and the multiplier of '16' will have to be applied.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.2,30,400/- (Rs.8,000 x 12 x 16 x 15%) towards 'loss of future income'.
6. The Tribunal has not awarded any amount towards 'pain and suffering' and 'loss of amenities'.
Having regard to the fact the claimant had suffered an head injury, facial fracture and a fracture of the knee.

It would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards NC: 2024:KHC:45824 'pain and suffering', and a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.
7.
A sum of Rs.1,66,520/- awarded as medical expenses by the Tribunal, being based on documentary evidence, does not call for modification and is hence confirmed.
8. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards 'food, conveyance and attendant charges'.

Since the claimant was hospitalized for about 21 days, at Mangalore, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.35,000/- towards 'food, conveyance and attendant charges'
9.

The Tribunal has taken the laid up period as 6 months, since the income is now taken as Rs.8,000/-, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.48,000/- towards 'loss of income during the laid up period'.
Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:
